message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look table of the **long weekends** that Canadians will enjoy in 2023.  
(“Long weekend” means a three‑day stretch that includes a statutory holiday and at least one weekend day.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Observed (if different) | Long‑weekend span |
|---------|-------------|--------------------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (Sunday) | Jan 2 (Monday) | **Jan 1–3** |
| Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, BC, SK, MB) | Feb 20 (Monday) | – | **Feb 18–20** |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Friday) | – | **Apr 7–9** |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | – | **May 20–22** |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Saturday) | Jul 3 (Monday) | **Jul 1–3** |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Monday) | – | **Sep 2–4** |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 (Monday) | – | **Oct 7–9** |
| Christmas | Dec 25 (Monday) | – | **Dec 23–25** |

> **Note:**  
> - Some provinces observe Family Day on different dates (e.g., Quebec has St. Patrick’s Day on March 17).  
> - Remembrance Day (Nov 11) is observed on Nov 10 in most provinces, so it doesn’t create a long weekend in 2023.  
> - Boxing Day (Dec 26) is observed on Dec 27 in most provinces, so it also isn’t a long weekend.

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app!
